articles.title: ‘Os sentidos do trabalho: Ensaio sobre a afirmação e a negação do trabalho’ by Ricardo Antunes
articles.author: Editor
articles.content_excerpt: In 1999, the first edition of the Brazilian sociologist Ricardo Antunes’s The Meanings of Work [Os sentidos do trabalho] was published. Its stakes were clear: against the idea that new communication and automation technologies were announcing the “end of work”, Antunes insisted that work remained vital, both for capital and for humanity. articles.title: ICE is hiding detainees from their families – and the death toll is rising
articles.author: Zoe Alexandra
articles.content_excerpt: ICE just scrubbed tens of thousands of people from its Online Detainee Locator System, leaving their families and legal teams in the dark. Aaron Reichlin-Melnick, senior fellow at the American Immigration Council, joins Zoe Alexandra and Rania Khalek to break down how DHS effectively “disappeared” at least 20,000 people with final deportation orders, as deaths in custody climb and private prison giants GEO Group and CoreCivic rake in profits from ICE’s ballooning budget. articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 | Propaganda for US war in Korea?
articles.author: Amanda Yee
articles.content_excerpt: The new Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 just dropped, and it’s already mired in controversy. The game simulates urban warfare in Seoul, casting players as a South Korean marine fighting off an invasion from the DPRK. Is this video game harmless entertainment, or is it sophisticated imperialist propaganda designed to “manufacture consent” for war against North Korea and normalize US militarism? Ju-Hyun Park, organizer with Nodutdol for Korean Community Development and director of engagement at Breakthrough News, joins Amanda Yee to break down the dangerous political messaging behind Modern Warfare 4.
source_folders: 06_左派ニュース・社会主義戦略

articles.title: Congolese president signs referendum bill that could allow for a third-term
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Félix Tshisekedi has promulgated a controversial law establishing the conditions for holding referendums. Opposition parties, civil society groups and grassroots movements have previously said it could allow him to seek a third term. The signing follows more than five months of protests, court challenges, and street mobilization against the law. The promulgation was announced on national television late on Tuesday, November 10. “The President of the Republic, Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, promulgated, on November 10, 2026, through an ordinance, the law setting the conditions for the organization of the referendum in the Democratic Republic of Congo,” state broadcaster RTNC reported. articles.title: Keytruda was built on public science. Why does Merck own the rewards?
articles.author: David Franco
articles.content_excerpt: Keytruda is often presented as the ultimate success story of modern pharmaceutical innovation. And in one sense, that is true. Few medicines have transformed oncology as profoundly as pembrolizumab. It has extended survival in melanoma, lung cancer, and many other malignancies, and it has helped turn immune checkpoint inhibition from a scientific hypothesis into a clinical reality. For many patients, it has meant years of life that previously had few options at all. But that is only one part of the story. The other part is far less comfortable. Keytruda is not just a breakthrough drug.
